# Test 20261012-233357-d188: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | Turn 2; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44 | The customer asked, "Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210." The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`, creating `RS-381D78` and `RS-21C2D7`. It held 2 units, violating "A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more." The retry loop sends the second request even after the first succeeds. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; stock.json:6; stock.json:11; RULES.md:6 | The reply said, "I've reserved 1 teapot set for order 6210 with reservation ID RS-21C2D7." The backend and saved state show two reservations of `"qty": 1` for that order. The confirmation understates the total quantity held and omits the first reservation. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:16; stock.json:3 | The reply said, "You now have 2 units remaining in stock." The final reservation response has `"left": 1`, matching saved stock. The reply overstates available stock by one unit. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:28; trace.jsonl:24; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16 | The reply said, "It appears one additional unit was reserved or sold since your reservation." The stock tool returned only `{"sku": "teapot-set", "left": 1}` and supplied no transaction history or explanation. The recorded extra reservation occurred during turn 2 as part of the app's duplicate request; the record provides no support for an intervening reservation or sale. |

## Notes

The transcript begins "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Reviewed all 3 turns and 31 model items, findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, and seal.json. Findings were empty, and the audit reported no breaks, errors, or changed turn wording. Those checks do not establish business correctness.

Read RULES.md and all six Python source files. Checked current stock.json and state.json using read-only commands. Stock contains both recorded reservations for order 6210 and 1 remaining teapot set; state contains the three case notes. The current project state is outside the test seal, so it corroborates rather than replaces the sealed backend evidence. No app-state files were listed in the seal or matched the app-state file glob, so no sealed state snapshot was available.

The duplicate request is explained by services.py:44 through services.py:47, which repeat the POST after success. Each POST decrements stock and appends a reservation in stock.py:76 and stock.py:82. The reserve tool at app.py:72 returns only the last reservation and requested quantity, omitting remaining stock and the earlier hold. Turn 1 and the stock count in turn 3 agree with their tool results. The recorded tool names and model arguments fit the requests.

Did not start the app, send it messages, make new backend requests, or modify its state. Wrote only this report. No conclusions were drawn about untested return, refund, or privacy behavior.
